briefdescription.para: Constructs a test case with a name, runner, parent suite, index, nesting depth, and body.

detaileddescription.para: Private, since the index, the nesting depth, and the parent suite are internal; a test case constructed elsewhere would not be registered with its parent, and would never run.

name
The test case name or description, used in reports, and the location of the call to test() that created the test case.
test_runner
The test runner managing this test case.
parent_suite
The suite that owns this test case.
own_index
The one-based positional index within the parent.
nesting_depth
The depth of nesting; 1 for top-level test cases.
body
A reference to the body, with its arguments already bound, invoked when the test case executes; it must outlive the test case.
Stores the reference to the body, the location of the call to test(), the parent suite, and the nesting depth.

briefdescription.para: Aborts test execution via the owning runner, for a failed requirement.

detaileddescription.para: Private, since it is used only by the check result, a friend, for a failed requirement without exceptions; the user code calls runner::abort().

sl
The source location from which the abort is triggered.
Returns
Does not return.
Delegates to the private runner::abort(), as caused by a failed requirement, passing the supplied source location, so that the report identifies it. The runner then calls the abort handler, if any, and terminates the process via ::abort().

briefdescription.para: Reports an exception that escaped the test case body as a failed check.

detaileddescription.para: The failure is reported at the location of the call to test() that created the test case, since the location of the throw is not known.

what
The explanatory string of a std::exception, or nullptr for an exception of another type.
Returns
Nothing.
The failure is reported as a check: the test point number is incremented first, as check_result does, so that the TAP output numbers it after the checks already reported, and the failed checks counter is incremented, so that the test case, and through it its parents, fail.

The message is unexpected exception: followed by what, or unexpected exception of unknown type when what is nullptr; the type of a std::exception is not shown, since its name is available only via RTTI, and only in an implementation-defined (usually mangled) form. There is no expression to display.

briefdescription.para: Executes the test case body by invoking the referred callable.

detaileddescription.para: Private, since the test case is run only once, by after_test_case_create(), right after its creation.

Always inlined there, with a non-virtual call, so that, without optimisations, it adds no frame to the call chain of each nested test case; the out-of-line copy is used only through the virtual table.

Parameters
None.
Returns
Nothing.
Invokes the referred body with this test case, surrounded by reporter calls to begin and end the test case.

When exceptions are enabled, an exception that escapes the callable is caught and reported as a failed check of this test case, and the test case ends normally, so that the run continues with the next test case; the checks performed before the exception remain reported. Since the nested test cases catch their own exceptions, an exception is reported by the innermost test case whose body it escapes.
The detail::failed_requirement exception, thrown after a failed require(), only stops the body; the failure was already reported and counted.

An exception thrown by the abort handler, after the abort of the test execution was reported, is passed on, without reporting it, and without ending the test case, since the report is already complete; it reaches the application, which set the handler to return control this way.
Defined here, as inline, so that it can be always inlined into after_test_case_create().

briefdescription.para: Deleted copy constructor to prevent copying.

briefdescription.para: Adds a nested test case for each value of a range or a tuple, and runs them.

detaileddescription.para: For each value, in order, a test case is added and run, as by test(), with the value as the argument of the callable, which is called as callable (test_case, value). The values may be a range (a container, an array, a span, or a view), or a tuple, whose values may have different types, for a generic callable:

Each test case is named after the common name, followed by the value in parentheses, written as in the messages of the checks (Sizes (16)); a value that cannot be written (see extension::printable), such as an application type without an operator<<, is replaced by its position, starting at 1 (Records (#2)). The location of all the test cases is that of the call.

briefdescription.para: Gets the totals of the node.

detaileddescription.para: The reference is read-only, for the const and the non-const nodes alike, so that a test case or a suite cannot modify its own counters, which decide the exit code. The counters are updated only by the framework, which accesses the protected member directly.

Parameters
None.
A const reference to the counters instance.
Returns a const reference to the counters member.

briefdescription.para: The number of direct child test cases.

detaileddescription.para: Incremented for each call to test(), which creates a child test_case and runs it immediately. The child test cases are not kept after they run, so that the memory does not grow with the number of test cases; only their number is needed later, for the TAP plan.

briefdescription.para: The node name.

detaileddescription.para: Not owned; it points to a string whose lifetime exceeds that of the node. Derived classes may access this member directly, in addition to the public name() getter.

briefdescription.para: The test index, counting from 1.

detaileddescription.para: The position of this object within its parent, displayed by the TAP reporter in the ok/not ok lines. Set directly by the runner, which numbers the suites when it runs them, and by the top suite, which, when added, is always the first one.

briefdescription.para: Reference to the test runner that owns this object.

detaileddescription.para: Provides access to the reporter, to the filter, and to the state of the session (the running test case, and the abort and listing flags), and is used when aborting.

briefdescription.para: The number of the most recent child test point.

detaileddescription.para: Test points are numbered from 1; the value is 0 before the first one. This number counts the checks and the nested test cases of this object, in execution order, as required by the TAP ok/not ok lines. It is incremented for each check (by the check result) and for each nested test case created.

briefdescription.para: Totals for the node.

detaileddescription.para: For the suites, the totals include the checks of all their test cases; for a test case, they include only its own checks, plus the counts of its direct nested test cases.

The check counters are updated by the check result, which is a friend; the test case counters by after_test_case_create(), when a nested test case ends. For a suite, the totals of each of its test cases are also added, by the same function.

briefdescription.para: Counts a newly constructed child test case and executes it immediately.

detaileddescription.para: The child test case is a local object of create_test_case(), and is destroyed when that function returns.

test_case
The newly created test_case.
suite
The parent suite to which execution results are reported.
Returns
Nothing.
Counts test_case, which is a local object of the calling create_test_case(), and immediately invokes test_case::run() on it. The test case is not kept; only child_test_cases_count_ is needed later, for the TAP plan.

If the filter patterns do not select the test case (its own name at its nesting level, or the name of suite at level 0, which matters only for the top suite, since the other suites run only when selected), its body is not called: the reporter is notified with skip_test_case() and the parent's skipped test cases counter is incremented. The test case keeps its index and its place among the children, so the TAP plan of the parent remains complete.

Otherwise, while the test case runs, the runner keeps it as its innermost running test case (see suite::test()). The parent's executed test cases counter is incremented after the run, and, if the child failed (a failed check, or a failed nested test case), its failed test cases counter too, so that the parent fails as well, as in node-tap. The child's check counters are intentionally not merged into the parent totals; each test case reports only its own counters. The child's totals are, however, accumulated into suite so that the suite summary reflects all checks performed by its test cases.
While the test cases are listed (see runner_options::list_tests), the selected test case is listed by the runner, and neither run nor counted, except in child_test_cases_count_.
After the test execution was aborted (possible only when the abort handler threw an exception, which the application caught), the report is complete, so the test case is neither run nor reported.

memberdef.name: create_test_case

briefdescription.para: Creates a child test case, and runs it.

detaileddescription.para: The common body of suite::test() and test_case::test(), which differ only in the parent suite and the nesting depth of the test cases they create.
Always inlined into them, even without optimisations, since each nested test case adds one call chain to the stack, and a separate frame for this function would make it longer.

Callable_T
The type of a callable object.
Args_T
The types of the callable arguments.
name
The test case name or description, used in reports, and the location of the call to test().
parent_suite
The suite to which the test case belongs.
nesting_depth
The depth of nesting of the test case; 1 for the direct children of a suite.
callable
A generic callable object, usually a lambda, invoked to perform the test.
arguments
A possibly empty list of arguments to be passed to the callable.
Returns
Nothing.
Binds the callable and its arguments into a local body, constructs the child test_case as a local object that refers to the body, with the next test point number of this node as its index, then passes it to after_test_case_create(), which counts and runs it.

The child test case and its body, with the copies of the arguments, are destroyed when this function returns, so the memory used by a test session does not grow with the number of test cases; the stack holds one test case and one body for each level of nesting being run. Since the body is not stored in a std::function, it is never allocated, whatever the size of the lambda captures and of the arguments.

true once runner::abort() was called.

briefdescription.para: A named, runnable test case that lives inside a suite.

detaileddescription.para: test_case represents a single, named test case or a nested group of checks within a parent suite or test_case. It is constructed by calling suite::test() or test_case::test(), both of which create the object, immediately execute its callable body via run(), and register the result with the parent node. The object is local to the test() call, and is destroyed when it returns, together with the body and the copies of its arguments, which are also local to that call; the test case only refers to them, so no memory is allocated for them.

The body of the test case is supplied as a callable (typically a lambda) that receives a test_case& reference as its first argument. Inside the body, expect() and require() are used to evaluate conditions and record the results. Test cases may be nested to an arbitrary depth.
The constructor is private, since its parameters are set by the framework; the test cases are created only by suite::test() and test_case::test().
The class is non-copyable and non-movable to preserve unique ownership and consistent state throughout the test session.
